title: Design app architecture and component structure
description: Based on research findings, design the app architecture: 1) Choose UI framework (Compose vs XML) 2) Define data flow pattern 3) Plan component hierarchy 4) Document technical decisions

comments.author: android
comments.text:
## Architecture Design: Browser Chooser App

### Package Structure
```
com.browserlauncher/
├── MainActivity.kt              # Entry point, handles incoming intents
├── data/
│   ├── model/
│   │   └── BrowserInfo.kt       # Data class for browser apps
│   ├── repository/
│   │   └── BrowserRepository.kt # Queries installed browsers
│   └── preferences/
│       └── UserPreferences.kt   # DataStore for user settings
├── ui/
│   ├── theme/
│   │   ├── Theme.kt             # Material 3 theme
│   │   ├── Color.kt             # Color definitions
│   │   └── Type.kt              # Typography
│   ├── picker/
│   │   ├── BrowserPickerScreen.kt    # Main picker composable
│   │   ├── BrowserPickerViewModel.kt # State management
│   │   └── BrowserListItem.kt        # Single browser row
│   └── settings/
│       └── SettingsScreen.kt    # Settings/preferences UI
└── util/
    └── IntentUtils.kt           # Intent creation helpers
```

### Data Flow
1. User clicks link in external app
2. Android routes to MainActivity (registered as browser)
3. MainActivity extracts URL from intent
4. BrowserRepository queries installed browsers
5. BrowserPickerScreen displays list
6. User taps browser -> launch intent forwarded
7. Optional: Save preference if 'always use' checked

### Key Technical Decisions
- **UI**: Jetpack Compose (not XML)
- **State**: ViewModel + StateFlow
- **Storage**: DataStore Preferences
- **Theme**: Material 3 with dynamic colors
- **Min SDK**: 23 (keep current)
- **No DI framework**: Simple app, manual injection sufficient

## Data Models

### BrowserInfo
```kotlin
data class BrowserInfo(
    val packageName: String,        // e.g., 'com.android.chrome'
    val activityName: String,       // Full component name
    val label: String,              // Display name 'Chrome'
    val icon: Drawable,             // App icon
    val isDefault: Boolean = false  // User's saved default
)
```

### UserPreferences (DataStore)
```kotlin
data class UserPreferences(
    val defaultBrowserPackage: String? = null,  // Saved default
    val alwaysAsk: Boolean = true,              // Show picker every time
    val lastUsedPackage: String? = null         // For sorting
)
```

### UI State
```kotlin
sealed class PickerUiState {
    object Loading : PickerUiState()
    data class Success(
        val browsers: List<BrowserInfo>,
        val url: String,
        val showAlwaysUseOption: Boolean = true
    ) : PickerUiState()
    data class Error(val message: String) : PickerUiState()
    object NoBrowsers : PickerUiState()  // Edge case
}
```

## UI Components Design

### Screen Layout (ModalBottomSheet style)
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│  ══════════════════════════     │ <- Drag handle
│                                 │
│  Open with...                   │ <- Title
│  example.com/path               │ <- URL preview (truncated)
│                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ [icon] Chrome           │    │ <- BrowserListItem
│  └─────────────────────────┘    │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ [icon] Firefox          │    │
│  └─────────────────────────┘    │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ [icon] Brave            │    │
│  └─────────────────────────┘    │
│                                 │
│  ☐ Always use this browser      │ <- Checkbox option
│                                 │
│  [ CANCEL ]                     │ <- Secondary action
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Composable Hierarchy
```
BrowserPickerActivity (ComponentActivity)
└── BrowserPickerTheme
    └── ModalBottomSheet
        └── BrowserPickerContent
            ├── DragHandle
            ├── Header (title + url)
            ├── LazyColumn
            │   └── BrowserListItem (repeated)
            ├── AlwaysUseCheckbox
            └── CancelButton
```

### BrowserListItem
- Icon (48dp) | Label | Ripple effect on tap
- Highlight if isDefault
- Material 3 ListItem component

comments.text:
## Manifest Configuration

### Required Intent Filters
```xml
<!-- Browser picker activity -->
<activity android:name=".ui.picker.BrowserPickerActivity"
    android:exported="true"
    android:theme="@style/Theme.BrowserLauncher.Transparent"
    android:excludeFromRecents="true">
    
    <!-- Register as browser for http/https -->
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
        <data android:scheme="http" />
        <data android:scheme="https" />
    </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

### Package Visibility Queries
```xml
<queries>
    <!-- Query for browser apps -->
    <intent>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
        <data android:scheme="http" />
    </intent>
    <intent>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
        <data android:scheme="https" />
    </intent>
</queries>
```

## Build Dependencies (build.gradle.kts additions)
```kotlin
// Compose BOM
implementation(platform("androidx.compose:compose-bom:2024.02.00"))
implementation("androidx.compose.material3:material3")
implementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui")
implementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling-preview")
debugImplementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling")

// ViewModel + Compose integration
implementation("androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel-compose:2.7.0")
implementation("androidx.activity:activity-compose:1.8.2")

// DataStore
implementation("androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences:1.0.0")

// Coroutines (already present)
implementation("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-android:1.7.3")
```

### Compose Compiler Configuration
```kotlin
buildFeatures {
    compose = true
}
composeOptions {
    kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion = "1.5.8"
}
```

comments.text:
## Research Findings: Android 12+ Link Handling

### Problem Statement
Android 12+ changed how web links are handled. The system no longer shows an app picker for http/https links - instead, links go directly to the user's default browser.

### Key Technical Findings

**1. Web Intent Resolution Changes (Android 12+)**
- Generic web intents resolve to user's default browser by default
- Apps must use Android App Links with domain verification to bypass this
- The disambiguation dialog no longer appears for unverified domains

**2. Required Manifest Configuration for Browser App**
Must include CATEGORY_APP_BROWSER to register as browser:
- ACTION: android.intent.action.VIEW
- CATEGORY: android.intent.category.DEFAULT
- CATEGORY: android.intent.category.BROWSABLE
- CATEGORY: android.intent.category.APP_BROWSER (key for browser registration)
- DATA: http and https schemes

**3. Package Visibility (Android 11+)**
Must declare queries in manifest to use queryIntentActivities():
- Add <queries> element with intent for VIEW action + http/https schemes
- Without this, queryIntentActivities returns empty list

**4. Browser Picker App Strategy**
1. Register as default browser using CATEGORY_APP_BROWSER
2. Intercept all http/https intents
3. Query installed browsers via PackageManager
4. Present custom picker UI
5. Forward intent to selected browser

### Sources
- developer.android.com/about/versions/12/behavior-changes-12
- developer.android.com/training/package-visibility

comments.text:
## Research Findings: Modern Android Architecture 2025

### UI Framework Decision: Jetpack Compose
**Recommendation: Use Jetpack Compose** (not XML layouts)

Rationale:
- Google's official recommended UI toolkit
- Declarative paradigm = simpler state management
- 40-60% less boilerplate code
- Better performance with smart recomposition
- Future-proof choice for new projects

### Architecture Patterns

**Recommended Stack:**
- UI: Jetpack Compose with Material Design 3
- Architecture: MVVM with ViewModel + StateFlow
- DI: Hilt (or skip for simple app)
- Async: Kotlin Coroutines + Flow
- Storage: DataStore Preferences

**UI Pattern:**
- ModalBottomSheet for picker (Material 3)
- LazyColumn for browser list
- StateFlow for reactive state

### Minimum Dependencies
- compose-bom for version alignment
- material3 for M3 components
- lifecycle-viewmodel-compose
- datastore-preferences

### DataStore vs SharedPreferences
DataStore recommended: async, type-safe, coroutine-based
SharedPreferences is legacy and can cause ANRs

### Sources
- developer.android.com/jetpack/compose
- m3.material.io
- developer.android.com/topic/architecture
